exposure: CHD classification based on expected fetal brain oxygen delivery (Class A: expected oxygen supply, Class B: expected normal oxygen supply)
outcome: dimensions of infratentorial brain structures (cerebellar vermis craniocaudal diameter, anteroposterior diameter, circumference, area; trans-cerebellar diameter; pons, midbrain, medulla oblongata anteroposterior diameters)
cohort: A total of 112 singleton pregnancies between 28 and 34 weeks of gestation were enrolled, comprising 56 fetuses with congenital heart disease and 56 healthy controls.
finding: Fetuses with congenital heart disease exhibited significant reductions in specific infratentorial brain measurements, including cerebellar vermis dimensions and brainstem structures (pons and medulla oblongata), compared to healthy controls, regardless of their classification based on expected cerebral oxygen delivery.
cross-section timing: Between 28 and 34 weeks of gestation for neurosonographic evaluation
birth_weight: 3121 ± 477 g (CHD group) and 3336 ± 318 g (control group) at delivery
gest_age: 28-34 weeks of gestation (at enrollment for neurosonographic evaluation); 38.23 ± 1.41 weeks (CHD group) and 38.87 ± 1.19 weeks (control group) at delivery
